entities.summary: Dame Carole Jordan, was a British physicist, astrophysicist, astronomer and academic. She was Professor Emeritus of Astrophysics at the University of Oxford and Emeritus Fellow at Somerville College, Oxford. From 1994 to 1996, she was President of the Royal Astronomical Society; she was the first woman to hold this position. She won the Gold Medal of the Royal Astronomical Society in 2005; she was only the third female recipient following Caroline Herschel in 1828 and Vera Rubin in 1996. She was head of the Rudolf Peierls Centre for Theoretical Physics at the University of Oxford from 2003 to 2004 and 2005 to 2008, and was one of the first female professors in Astronomy in Britain.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As President of the Royal Astronomical Society and a leading figure in British astronomy, Dame Carole Jordan played a crucial role in promoting women's participation in STEM fields, paving the way for future generations of female astronomers. Her contributions to the field have had a lasting impact on our understanding of the universe.
